historic/u3e5/battle-of-lexington.jpg.description: Amos Doolittle's engraving of the Battle of Lexington, April 19, 1775: minutemen on the green at dawn, eight Americans dead within minutes.

historic/u3e5/burgoyne-reynolds.jpg.description: General John Burgoyne, whose march from Canada collapsed at Saratoga, by Joshua Reynolds.

historic/u3e5/crisis-museum.jpg.description: Paine's works at the Museum of the American Revolution: Common Sense and The American Crisis, read to the troops in December 1776.

historic/u3e5/de-grasse-statue.jpg.description: Statue of the Comte de Grasse: his fleet sealed the Chesapeake.

historic/u3e5/death-of-warren.jpg.description: John Trumbull's Death of General Warren at the Battle of Bunker's Hill, June 17, 1775 — fought on Breed's Hill, not Bunker Hill.

historic/u3e5/franklin-1767.jpg.description: Benjamin Franklin, who worked the French court from late 1776 to win the alliance of 1778.

historic/u3e5/horatio-gates-stuart.jpg.description: Horatio Gates, the American commander at Saratoga, by Gilbert Stuart.

historic/u3e5/lafayette-yorktown.jpg.description: Lafayette at Yorktown, commanding American troops at twenty-four.

historic/u3e5/nathanael-greene-trumbull..description: Nathanael Greene, who bled Cornwallis's army at Cowpens and Guilford Courthouse and slipped away before it could be destroyed, by John Trumbull.

historic/u3e5/steuben-valley-forge.jpg.description: Baron von Steuben at Valley Forge, 1777, from the National Archives: drilling the barefoot army into professionals.

historic/u3e5/treaty-of-alliance-signatu.description: Signatures on the 1778 Treaty of Alliance: French money, guns, troops, and eventually the navy entered the war.

historic/u3e5/washington-crossing-bingha.description: Washington Crossing the Delaware, by George Caleb Bingham: the Trenton surprise.

historic/u3e5/yorktown-surrender-met.jpg.description: The surrender of Cornwallis to Washington and Rochambeau at Yorktown, from the Metropolitan Museum.
